image.name: Pathway Power LLC
image.subsector: Utility-scale solar and battery storage development
image.description: Pathway Power LLC is a U.S. utility-scale solar and battery-storage developer and independent power producer with projects across SPP, MISO and other U.S. power markets. Company and transaction materials describe a multi-gigawatt pipeline spanning 13 states, including the Greenridge hybrid solar-and-storage project in Texas and the Foxtrot battery project in Arkansas. Igneo Infrastructure Partners completed a preferred-equity investment on June 4, 2026 through its North American strategy and discloses joint governance and a board seat; the legal vehicle, ownership percentage and preference economics are not public. Pathway Power Holdings LLC is treated as a same-platform financing issuer, while Greenridge, Foxtrot and other project SPVs remain subordinate assets. Renova's convertible notes had not converted, and Forest Road, Rabobank and AB CarVal were evidenced as lenders rather than current ordinary-equity owners. No later platform sale, Igneo exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Terra-Gen
image.subsector: Utility-scale wind, solar, and battery storage
image.description: Terra-Gen develops, owns and operates utility-scale wind, solar and battery-storage assets across the United States. Public disclosures through July 2026 describe approximately 4.2 GW of gross operating capacity, 5.6 GWh of storage, 34 sites and a roughly 16 GW development pipeline. Terra-Gen Power Holdings II, LLC is the parent platform, Terra-Gen, LLC is the operating business and individual project SPVs remain subordinate assets. Current legal ownership is 50% through Igneo Infrastructure Partners' Global Diversified Infrastructure Fund chain and 50% through Masdar's acquisition chain. ArcLight formed the platform in 2007, Global Infrastructure Partners invested in 2009, Energy Capital Partners acquired it in 2015 and used a 2021 continuation vehicle for its retained 50% before Masdar closed its purchase on October 1, 2024. Pantheon Infrastructure Plc committed to a Terra-Gen-specific co-investment through an Igneo-managed vehicle in June 2026, but closing, funding, the security and stake were not publicly confirmed; Igneo remains recorded at 50% pending evidence. No later corporate ownership change or signed exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Mesteño Wind Project
image.description: Mesteño Wind Project is a 201.6 MW onshore wind facility in Starr County, Texas, commonly described as a 202 MW project. The facility comprises 56 Vestas V136-3.6 MW turbines, began commercial operation in 2019 and participates in the ERCOT market. InfraRed Capital Partners acquired the project company, Mesteno Windpower, LLC, from Duke Energy through Mesteno Aggregator LLC on May 29, 2024. Current regulatory records show InfraRed Energy Transition Fund A LP holding 3.48% directly in the aggregator and InfraRed Energy Transition Fund B LP holding 96.52% indirectly through Mesteno HoldCo LLC. The two positions together represent 100% InfraRed-controlled ownership. No later owner exit or signed ownership change was identified through September 1, 2026.

image.name: Longroad Energy
image.description: Longroad Energy Holdings, LLC develops, owns and operates utility-scale wind, solar and battery-storage projects across the United States. The company was founded in 2016 and serves utilities, corporations and wholesale power markets through a development-to-ownership model that combines contracted offtake, asset management and project-level financing. Current economic ownership is held by Infratil, New Zealand Super Fund, Munich Re and Longroad management. Infratil reported a 42.5% economic interest at March 31, 2026, while its current investment page reports 42.0%; the same page reports New Zealand Super Fund at 34.8%, Longroad management at 13.0% and Munich Re at 9.7%. Morrison manages or advises the Infratil and New Zealand Super Fund investments but is not itself recorded as a beneficial owner. MEAG manages Munich Re's interest through MR Hunu LP. No later company-level owner exit or signed ownership change was identified through September 1, 2026.

image.name: 38 Degrees North
image.subsector: Distributed generation, community solar, and battery storage
image.description: 38 Degrees North develops, owns, and operates distributed generation, community solar, battery storage, and related sustainable infrastructure assets. Its end markets include communities, development partners, capital providers, utilities, and commercial counterparties seeking distributed clean-energy solutions. The operating model combines development and ownership of physical energy assets with flexible capital partnerships, making it more infrastructure oriented than a software-only platform. Public materials describe a focus on community solar, distributed generation, and storage, and a July 2025 funding announcement stated that the company had raised more than $230 million of corporate growth capital and acquired U.S. Light Energy's 250 MW-plus pipeline. Kimmeridge made a growth equity investment alongside Climate Adaptive Infrastructure in 2025.

image.name: Coastal GasLink Pipeline
image.description: Coastal GasLink Pipeline Project is a 670-kilometre natural gas transmission project connecting northeastern British Columbia to LNG Canada’s export terminal in Kitimat. Its customers or end markets include LNG Canada and upstream natural gas production in the Montney region. The operating model is an asset-heavy transmission pipeline supported by long-term transportation arrangements rather than merchant commodity exposure. Operations are concentrated in British Columbia along the Dawson Creek-to-Kitimat corridor. Public materials indicate route length of 670 kilometres and design capacity of approximately 2.1 Bcf/d. Current ownership includes TC Energy, which retained 35% when KKR and AIMCo acquired a combined 65% interest in 2019; AIMCo’s exact split has not been publicly disclosed.

image.name: Pembina Gas Infrastructure Inc.
image.subsector: Gas processing, gathering and NGL extraction
image.description: Pembina Gas Infrastructure Inc. is a Western Canadian gas-processing and midstream platform serving producers in the Montney and Duvernay regions. Its fee-based infrastructure footprint extends from central Alberta to northeast British Columbia and includes 23 gas-processing facilities, approximately 3,900 kilometres of pipelines, more than 5 Bcf/d of processing capacity and approximately 330,000 barrels per day of NGL extraction capacity. Pembina owns 60% and operates the platform; Apollo-managed funds own the remaining 40% following their 2026 acquisition from KKR-managed infrastructure funds.

image.name: Port Arthur LNG
image.description: Port Arthur LNG is a two-phase liquefied-natural-gas export development in Jefferson County, Texas. Phase 1 comprises two liquefaction trains with approximately 13 Mtpa of nameplate capacity and is owned indirectly by KKR Denali (42%), Sempra Infrastructure Partners (28%) and ConocoPhillips (30%). Phase 2 adds approximately 13 Mtpa across two further trains and reached FID in September 2025; its direct legal members hold 50.1%, 40.0% and 9.9% interests, with KKR participating within the 40% member's parent consortium. The project is distinct from Sempra Infrastructure Partners, whose separate KKR-led platform transaction remained pending as of the latest verification.

image.name: Dames Point Jacksonville LLC
image.description: Dames Point Jacksonville LLC is the local operating and concession entity associated with JAXPORT's 158-acre Dames Point container terminal and adjacent intermodal container transfer facility in Jacksonville, Florida. The business handles container, stevedoring, crane, yard and rail-transfer activity for ocean carriers, cargo owners and military users under long-term port rights. Ceres acquired the former TraPac Jacksonville entity in 2022; Macquarie retained the renamed local SPV when the broader Ceres platform was sold to Carrix, then sold the Jacksonville business and assets separately to JAXPORT in November 2023. JAXPORT is the current owner and SSA is the contract operator, not an equity owner.

image.name: LBCT LLC
image.description: LBCT LLC operates the automated Long Beach Container Terminal at the Port of Long Beach's Middle Harbor/Pier E complex. The approximately 300-acre marine terminal provides vessel, yard, gate and on-dock rail handling for trans-Pacific container trade and has more than 3.5 million TEU of annual capacity. Olivia Holdings LLC acquired 100% of LBCT in October 2019 for US$1.78 billion. The current investor group includes Macquarie Infrastructure Partners IV, Munich Re through MEAG, Manulife/John Hancock and Rest; only Munich Re's 8.8% Olivia Holdings interest is publicly quantified, so the other consortium stakes remain explicitly undisclosed.
